subject: POC trial plan & model selection — Acme — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial plan & model selection — Acme — next steps

Hi Alice / Raj — great conversation this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

High-level goal:
- Validate that Redwood inference can meet Acme's accuracy, latency and cost targets for the customer-facing summarization + multilingual QA flow.

Success criteria (please confirm):
1) Quality: >85% helpfulness/accuracy on your curated eval set (English + Spanish + French).
2) Latency: P95 end-to-end generation < 600ms for single-turn summarization (95th percentile).
3) Throughput: sustained 20 rps peak for the trial workload (burst to 50 rps).
4) Cost: projected per-1k-token cost (hosted) within the threshold we discussed — we'll model during the trial.

Evaluation plan:
- You provide ~500 representative prompts + expected outputs (labels) for the eval harness. Raj to confirm dataset location and access.
- Redwood will run a fixed harness across candidate open models and quantization configs and return a results matrix (accuracy, latency, tokens, cost).
- We'll run operator-facing logs and per-token latency traces so we can tune batching/kv-cache usage.

Model selection (initial):
- Primary recommendation: Llama-2-Chat-70B (quantized to 4-bit where possible) — best quality for long-form summarization and multilingual behavior.
- Fallback / cost-optimized: Llama-2-13B (4-bit) and Mistral-Instruct-7B for low-cost baseline.
- If we see Spanish/French degradation, we will add a lightweight reranker or run the smaller model for those languages depending on quality/cost tradeoffs.

Security / data handling:
- For the trial we can use our hosted sandbox with customer data isolation. If you require VPC/Private deployment we can switch to Private mode later in the engagement. Marissa attached the SOC2 attestation for reference.

Timeline (proposed):
- 2/20: Kickoff + access handoff (S3 + sample eval set).
- 2/20–3/05: Trial / evaluation window (2 weeks).
- 3/03: Mid-trial sync (preliminary results, tuning).
- 3/10: Final review + next-step decision (Dedicated/private or scale).

Ownership / asks:
- Redwood: Ben (lead) and Marissa (infrastructure/ops). We'll run the benchmark harness and delivery.
- Acme: Raj to provide sample dataset, S3 access, and a single technical contact for onboarding.

Attachments: ACME_POC_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), model_benchmarks_q2.csv (example format).

Please confirm the success criteria above and whether the model choices look good — if so we'll schedule the kickoff for 2/20 and I'll send a calendar invite + the MAP to sign.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: POC trial plan & model selection — Acme — next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick notes/questions: 

- Success criteria look good overall. For quality, can we define the measurement more specifically (e.g., top-1 exact match vs. human-judged helpfulness)? We can provide both labeled answers and a small human eval set.
- Multilingual: Spanish is the priority; French is lower priority but nice to have. We will provide ~200 Spanish examples and ~50 French.
- Data/Privacy: we'll give you a scoped S3 bucket and temporary credentials for the trial. No PHI in the sample set.

Confirming 2/20 kickoff works for us. Can you also include an estimate for expected per-1k-token cost for each model candidate (rough ballpark) in your trial results?

Thanks — Alice

Acme Corp

Subject: Re: POC trial plan & model selection — Acme — next steps

Adding ops notes — thanks team.

- We'll prepare the benchmark harness and a runbook for how we test quantized variants (4-bit, 8-bit) and a baseline float run where feasible. I'll include Falcon-40B-instruct as an additional comparison since it often sits between Llama-2-13B and 70B in the quality/cost curve for some multilingual workloads.
- For latency tuning, we'll try a combination of smaller batch sizes + prefix KV caching for repeated user flows. If Acme needs guaranteed P95 SLAs we should discuss Dedicated node sizing after the trial.
- Attached: SOC2_Attestation.pdf (for procurement).

Next steps for Ops from Acme:
- Provide S3 role/creds to redwood-poc@redwood.com or add redwood-poc@redwood.com principal.
- Share the eval dataset (500 items ideally) in the agreed schema.

I'll start preparing the infra and will share the initial benchmark matrix by 2/25.
